To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) time to takeoff of new product varies substantially across provinces in China; (2) this intra-country variation is explained by economic institutions and product network characteristics.

(1) the average time to new product takeoff varies substantially across Chinese provinces and (2) the intra-country differences are explained by economic wealth, trade, education, media, and transportation infrastructure; network externalities; and the year of introduction.

(a) there is a large intra-country difference in the takeoff of a product across provinces of China, (b) these differences are explained by economic institutions and network externalities of products, (c) these differences have been converging over time, and (d) a waterfall strategy might be more profitable than a wave strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of product diffusion and the role of institutional factors.
the dynamics of new product adoption across provinces within one country.
the takeoff of products in China and how this takeoff varies across provinces and over time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
China is not uniform in terms of takeoff of new product.
China is not a uniform country in terms of the takeoff of products, and that the intra-country differences are substantial, rivaling or even exceeding inter-country differences.
the time to takeoff of a new product in China is driven by a combination of institutional variables, product characteristics, and the time of introduction of the product.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the takeoff of a new product in a province of China is driven by the economic institutions in the province, the network externalities of the product, and the time of introduction.
the takeoff of a new product in a province is determined by the economic institutions and product network externality.
the time to takeoff of new product varies dramatically across provinces, converging across time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intra-country heterogeneity in the takeoff of a new product is substantial and that it varies with product characteristics and economic institutional variables.
intra-country diversity is often overlooked and may be as high or even greater than inter-country diversity.
intra-country heterogeneity may be as large as inter-country heterogeneity in some regions of the world, thus, calling for more research in this direction.
